$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every literal that more than one of needle-guide, needle-simulator and scl3300-stream has to agree on. Edited here and nowhere else: gen/ts/constants.ts and gen/py/needle_protocol/constants.py are generated from this file by tools/gen.sh and CI fails on any drift. A value that only one repo uses does NOT belong here.

ANGLE_STREAM_DEFAULT_PORT.description: Default listen port for needle-guide's output-only inclination WebSocket. Unassigned by IANA and outside the ephemeral range. Deliberately NOT TRACKER_WS_PORT: the two servers run on the same operator machine, so sharing a port means whichever binds second fails, and an operator who points one URL at the other reaches a real server streaming a protocol the subscriber cannot read -- which is how a healthy-looking OPEN socket ends up showing nothing.

TRACKER_WS_PORT.description: Port the needle-simulator Jetson tracker's WebSocket listens on. Named here so needle-guide can refuse to default onto it and so needle-simulator can diagnose a sensor URL that collides with it.

HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS.description: Gap between angle-stream heartbeats. Fast enough that HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS is four consecutive misses, so an ordinary scheduling hiccup in either process cannot be mistaken for a dead app; slow enough to be free against a sensor stream ticking at up to 62.5 Hz.

ANGLE_STALE_MS.description: How old the last angle frame may be before a subscriber stops calling it live. The sensor is silent while idle, so 'no angle for a while' is its resting state, not a fault: long enough to ride out the gap between samples, short enough that a needle put down mid-procedure stops reporting before anyone acts on it.

HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS.description: How old the last heartbeat may be before the link counts as gone. Larger than ANGLE_STALE_MS on purpose: a stale angle with a live link is a sensor sitting still, which the operator fixes by picking the needle up; a stale heartbeat is a dead link, which they fix at the cable. Collapsing them into one message sends the operator to the wrong end.

DUAL_EMIT_SUPPRESS_MS.description: Window within which a canonical `inclination` frame supersedes a deprecated `theta` one. Equal to ANGLE_STALE_MS by arithmetic, not by meaning: once the native side has been quiet longer than the staleness window there is nothing left to supersede and the legacy frame is the only angle on offer.

CONSOLE_THETA_VERTICAL_DEG.description: The CT console's theta for a perfectly vertical needle. Its scale runs theta = CONSOLE_THETA_VERTICAL_DEG - inclination, so this single number ties the two conventions. It is the ONLY place the two scales are allowed to meet; see angles/SPEC.md.

ON_TARGET_TOLERANCE_DEG.description: Half-width of the band a display calls 'on target': the needle visual, the ambient glow and the laser switch to the on-target colour when the absolute inclination error is below this. Display tolerance ONLY -- needle-guide's guidance audio has its own, separate, inclusive boundary that happens to share the number, and coupling them would silently change what the operator hears the next time either is tuned.

DEVICE_HANDSHAKE_CMD.description: Plain (non-NDJSON) line the host writes to a candidate serial port to ask it who it is. The host appends a newline before writing.

DEVICE_HANDSHAKE_REPLY_REGEX.description: Grammar of the reply: RESP:<NAME>_V<major>. Group 1 is the firmware name, group 2 the decimal major. The name group is greedy but backtracks, so SCL3300_STREAM_V1 splits as ('SCL3300_STREAM', 1) and not ('SCL3300', ...). A host MUST parse and check the major rather than string-equal the whole line: matching the full literal is the same thing today and stops working the moment the major moves, which is precisely when a wrong-protocol device must be refused loudly.

DEVICE_HANDSHAKE_NAME.description: Name the current firmware answers with. Deliberately the FIRMWARE's own name, not a host product's, so a second host can identify the same device without pretending to be the first.

DEVICE_HANDSHAKE_LEGACY_NAME.description: Name the pre-2026-09 firmware answers with, when it named the host product instead of itself. Accepted for as long as an un-reflashed Pico is still in the field; connecting to one logs a deprecation notice. This entry retires with the last such device.

DEVICE_HANDSHAKE_SUPPORTED_MAJOR.description: The only handshake major the current hosts implement. A device announcing another major speaks a wire format no host here implements, so it is refused at discovery instead of being connected and silently mis-parsed.

TRACKER_SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS.description: Tracker hello `protocol_version` values the desktop client can read. Two entries because the desktop is upgraded BEFORE the Jetson -- the rig needs a separate, human-run redeploy -- so a v2 desktop necessarily talks to a v1 rig until that happens. Drop 1 once every rig in service reports 2.
